title: Paint clocks
blurb: A loading effect that runs while a <progress> bar has no value, a card that beats with the caret, a scene placed from a video's currentTime, and a flag that moves one step for each frame of an animated GIF. The element's own repaints are the only clock: no requestAnimationFrame() and no timer.
question: Can the repaints of an element (an indeterminate progress bar, a caret, a video, an animated image) be the only clock for a canvas effect, with no requestAnimationFrame(), timer or requestPaint() loop?
result: Yes for all four. Measured paint rates in Chromium 157: 60 per second from a CSS-animated bar, 8 from the browser's own bar, 2 from a caret, 30 from a 30 fps video, and the frame rate of the GIF. Each effect stops when its element stops. Drawing an element at a new place raises a second paint event, so a handler has to read changedElements to tell the clock's events from those.
